memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"On that day tell your son, 'I do this because of what the LORD did for me when
I came out of Egypt.'" - Ex 13:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look closely at the words God puts in the parent's mouth. "What the LORD did for
me when I came out of Egypt."

Not "for your grandfather." Not "for our people long ago." For me.

Here is the striking thing. God intends this to be said by generations who were
never in Egypt at all. A father in the time of David, five hundred years later,
was still to say "when I came out." He was to speak of the exodus as his own
rescue, because he belonged to the people God had rescued.

That is not dishonesty. It is identity. What God did for His people, He did for
every member of them.

There is a lesson for parents and grandparents here that is easy to miss.
Children are rarely gripped by history. They are gripped by testimony. "This is
what God did for me" carries a weight that "this is what Christians believe"
never will.

You do not need a dramatic story. You need a true one. Tell your children what
God has actually done in your life, including the parts where you failed and He
was faithful anyway.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can you say clearly what God has done for you?
2. Who have you never told?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me to speak of what You have done for me, not just what I believe
about You. Give me courage to tell the next generation. Amen.
